items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: So we worked out the contract, and rather than come back to Los Angeles I formed a trio with Sir Charles Thompson on piano and Louis Gonsales.

ctx.x: Oh, no, we alternated with everybody. But the hours... We played three or four sets a night. But just standing around in between was, you know, pretty terrible. And I found out later that Leonard Feather lived upstairs over it at Number 2 Sheridan Square; he lived right over the place. That's I guess when he had... He was relatively new here then, too.

So we worked out the contract, and rather than come back to Los Angeles I formed a trio with Sir Charles Thompson on piano and Louis Gonsales. I hadn't mentioned him, but he was a guitarist in Lee and Lester's band. I hadn't mentioned who was in the band either. It was Paul Campbell, trumpet; Bumps Myers, Hubert Myers, tenor and Lester, tenor; and Jimmy Rowles was playing piano. But Benny Goodman stole Jimmy Rowles from us, so when we went in to New York, Clyde Hart came into the band and did the whole engagement…

items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: we didn't have anything to do so Red Calendar formed a trio with me and the guitar player

ctx.x: So any way I spent that time there with Lester Young and all these things were very enjoyable. Would you believe it, after the band disbanded, there was no more work for the band, and I think Lee perhaps went back to California, and I think Lester got took a vacation or something, and we didn't have anything to do so Red Calendar formed a trio with me and the guitar player, you know.
Can't you remember that guitar player's name yet?
